prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "build", with the standing line "The per-project folder of templates and assets that turns your app's details into a Mac bundle and a Windows build." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows Three shallow open trays drawn in section, stacked like drawers of one cabinet: the macOS tray, the Windows tray, and beneath them an empty output tray. From the macOS tray two identical plist sheets rise, each printed with empty ruled slots. A stream of small tags — product name, version, bundle identifier, copyright, icon — flows in from the left and drops one tag into each empty slot, so the left sheet is blank and the right sheet is filled. Filled sheets and the Windows items then descend by arrows into the empty output tray.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, a single empty slot on a sheet closing around the product name tag. circle two, the two plists side by side, one tagged to wails build, one to wails dev, the dev sheet carrying an extra permission for local networking. circle three, a document extension and its own small icon appearing on the sheet only when declared. circle four, a URL scheme entry appearing only when declared.

Colour is used so that warm orange marks the app details flowing in from the project. Teal marks template slots still empty. Deep grey-blue marks finished, shippable output.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: three folders inside build; two plist files, one for building and one for dev; four Windows build files; two target platforms; minimum macOS 10.13; two optional blocks.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: build on the cabinet; Info.plist and Info.dev.plist on the two rising sheets; wails build and wails dev on their arrows; icon.ico, info.json, the app manifest and installer files on the four Windows studies; file associations and custom URL scheme on their circles; the output folder on the lowest tray.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: build, macOS files, Windows files, the output folder, Info.plist, Info.dev.plist, product name, version, bundle identifier, copyright, app icon filled from project, wails build, wails dev, local networking, file associations, custom URL scheme icon.ico, info.json, the app manifest, installer files macOS app bundle, Windows installer, exe properties, high-resolution ready, minimum macOS delete to reset, rebuilt fresh, icon from source image

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Templates hold slots, not finished text; Your app's details fill every slot at build time. The dev sheet also permits local networking; Optional blocks appear only when you declare them. These four describe the app to Windows; The details pane reads what info.json holds. One folder, two platform-shaped results. Customise freely; deletion restores the default file; A missing icon is made from the source image.
